newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Taiwan sceptical of HK's future under China--poll.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sceptical of HK's future under China--poll.

text.p: Taiwan Chinese are more sceptical about Hong Kong's future under Chinese rule than their compatriots in the British-ruled territory which reverts to Beijing next week, a survey showed on Thursday.
The poll, conducted by Hong Kong University and Taiwan's World College of Journalism and Communications, interviewed 1,021 people in Hong Kong and 1,084 in Taiwan.

Less than eight percent in Taiwan believed China would honour its promise to the territory's 6.4 million people to leave their economic and political way of life unchanged for 50 years after the British pull out at midnight on June 30.
Almost 68 percent did not think China would keep its pledge.
In Hong Kong, almost 50 percent were confident Beijing would allow the territory a high degree of autonomy in running its own affairs, while 30 percent said no.
The survey also found Hong Kong people had a better impression of Taiwan, viewed by Beijing as a renegade province since the end of their civil war in 1949, than of China itself.
About 45 percent said they had a "good impression" of Taiwan, compared with 39 percent who did not.
As for China, 57.7 precent said they had a "bad impression" while 37 percent said they did not.
China sees the return of the 156-year-old British colony as a model for Taiwan's eventual reunification with the mainland.
